Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:1.hebrew: סורו רע - מנהגו רעה. קרבותו רע להשתדל עמו, שיהא סר אליו ובא לביתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:1.english: His conduct is bad - His conduct is bad. [Alternatively,] drawing near to him is bad, to deal with him such that one turns aside to him and enters his house.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:10.english: And the bathhouse attendant - One who heats bathhouses.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:2.hebrew: סורו רע - מנהגו רעה. קרבותו רע — להשתדל עמו שיהא סר אליו ובא לביתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:2.english: His practice is bad - His conduct is bad. [Alternatively,] associating with him is bad — [namely,] to deal with him such that he turns aside to him and comes into his house.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:3.hebrew: הצורפין - צורפי זהב העושין לנשים שירין, נזמים וטבעות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:3.english: The smiths - Goldsmiths who make bracelets, nose rings, and rings for women.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:4.hebrew: הסריקים - סורק בגדים לנשים, פלוקיירד"א (פלוקיידרי"ש: סורקי צמר):
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:4.english: The carders - [One who] combs garments for women, [in Old French:] floquiera (flochiedres: wool combers).

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:5.hebrew: הנקורות - מנקרי ריחים של יד, שנשים טוחנות בהם, כדתנן בכתובות (דף נט:): ״אלו מלאכות שהאשה עושה לבעלה: טוחנת ואופה״, ואמרינן (שם): בריחיא דידא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:5.english: The millstone groovers - Those who groove hand-mills with which women grind, as we learned in a mishna in Ketubot (59b): “These are the labors that a woman performs for her husband: She grinds and bakes”; and we say there: With a hand-mill.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:6.english: And the peddlers - [Those who] sell perfumed adornments to women.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:7.english: And the barbers - Women need them for their sons.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:8.hebrew: והגרע - אומן המקיז דם, על שם שמגרע את הדם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:8.english: And the bloodletter - A practitioner who lets blood, so called because he diminishes the blood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:11:9.english: The tanner - [One who] tans hides for them to wear [as garments] and to wear as shoes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:1.hebrew: מהלך על צידו ורוחו גסה ונתלה ויושב - שלשתן סימני גאוה, אבל אין זו דומה לזו, ובכולן הוא חלוק ממדת הכשרים. נתלה ויושב — אינו יושב אלא אם כן נסמך, או לאחוריו או על צידו, דרך גאוה. ובשביל שהבריות מוסרין נפשן לידו, הוא מתגאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:1.english: He walks on his side, and his spirit is arrogant, and he leans and sits - All three of them are signs of arrogance, but this one is not similar to that one, and in all of them he deviates from the conduct of upright people. [Regarding] "he leans and sits" — he does not sit unless he leans, either backward or on his side, in a haughty manner. And because people entrust their lives to his hand, he becomes conceited.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:2.hebrew: ועינו צרה - בממונו, להוציא כלום — מפני שהוא מלומד לאכול אצל המקיזין, ואינו מלומד להוציא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:2.english: And he is stingy - With his money, [unwilling] to spend anything, because he is accustomed to eating at [the homes of] those who undergo bloodletting, and is not accustomed to spending.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:3.hebrew: ועינו רעה - נותן עיניו בבריאים, שיחלו ויהיו צריכין לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:3.english: And his eye is evil - He casts his eyes upon healthy people, [hoping] that they fall ill and need him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:4.english: He eats much - For he is accustomed to eating with several people each day.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:5.hebrew: ומוציא קימעא - מתוך שמאכלו יפה, בלחם נקי ובשר שמן שממעטים את הזבל — שכל אדם מכין לסעודת הקזה מאכל בריאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:5.english: And discharges a little - Because his food is of fine quality — fine bread and fatty meat, which minimize bodily waste — for everyone prepares nourishing food for a bloodletting meal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:6.english: And suspected of forbidden relations - Since women need him and his occupation is with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:7.english: And of stealing - For women steal from their husbands and give [it] to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:12:8.english: And of bloodshed - Sometimes he drains his blood to less than a quarter-log [remaining].

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:1:1.hebrew: הכל לשם שמים - ואין דעתי אחריה לחיבת אישות, אלא לחיבת קורבה ולעשות קורת רוח לאמה כשאני מחבב את בתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:1:1.english: All is for the sake of Heaven - And my intention toward her is not for marital affection, but rather for familial affection, and to give satisfaction to her mother when I show affection to her daughter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:1.hebrew: לא ילמד רווק סופרים - רווק — פנוי בלא אשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:1.english: A bachelor may not act as a teacher of children - A bachelor — an unmarried man, without a wife.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:2.hebrew: סופרים - מלמדי תינוקות. כלומר, לא ירגיל רווק עצמו להיות מן הסופרים, ובגמר' מפרש טעמא. וכן "לא תלמד אשה סופרים" — לא תרגיל עצמה להיות ממלמדי תינוקות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:2.english: Scribes - Teachers of children. That is to say, an unmarried man should not accustom himself to be among the scribes, and in the Gemara the reason is explained. And likewise, "nor may a woman teach scribes" — she should not accustom herself to be among the teachers of children.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:3.english: Even one who does not have a wife - In the Gemara, it explains what this is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:4.english: A bachelor may not herd animals - Lest he lust after them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:5.english: Nor may two bachelors sleep with one covering - So that they do not come to [engage in] homosexual intercourse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:2:6.english: And the Sages permit [it] - For [Israel] are not suspected of homosexual intercourse or bestiality.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:1.hebrew: מ"ט - לא ילמד רווק סופרים? אי נימא משום דחשידי רווקים אמשכב זכור דתינוקות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:1.english: What is the reason - [That] a bachelor may not teach children? If we say [it is] because bachelors are suspected of homosexual intercourse with the children:

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:2.hebrew: אמרו לו לר' יהודה - דמתניתין, דאמר: לא יישנו שני רווקין בטלית אחת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:2.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda - [This refers to the Rabbi Yehuda] of our Mishnah, who said: "Two bachelors shall not sleep in one blanket."

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:3.hebrew: משום אמהתא דינוקי - אמותיהם של תינוקות, שמצויות אצלו להביא את בניהן לבית הספר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:3:3.english: Due to the mothers of the children - The mothers of the children, who are frequently with him to bring their sons to school.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:4:1.hebrew: מי שאין לו אשה כלל - ומוסיף אדתנא קמא, דקאמר: רווק — שלא נשא אשה מימיו, ואתא ר' אלעזר למימר: אפילו היתה לו ומתה, אבל יש לו ואינה שרויה אצלו — מותר; או דלמא כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:4:1.english: One who does not have a wife at all - And [does he] add to [the words of] the first Tanna, who said "a bachelor" — [meaning] one who never married a woman in his lifetime — and Rabbi Elazar came to say [that] even [if] he had [a wife] and she died [he may not teach], but [if] he has [a wife] and she is not residing with him, [it is] permitted; or perhaps, etc.?

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:1.hebrew: כל שעסקיו עם הנשים - שמלאכת אומנותו נעשית לנשים, והנשים צריכות לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:1.english: Anyone whose dealings are with women - That the work of his trade is done for women, and women have need of him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:2.hebrew: לא יתייחד עם הנשים - אפילו עם הרבה נשים, לפי שלבו גס בהו וכולן מחפות עליו. ואילו איש אחרינא — בין שתי נשים תנן (לעיל קידושין דף פ:), אבל עם שלש או ארבע שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:2.english: May not be secluded with women - Even with many women, since he is familiar with them and all of them cover for him. Whereas for another man, we learned [that the prohibition applies only] with two women (above, Kiddushin 80b), but with three or four, it is permitted.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:3.english: A clean and easy [trade] - It is explained well in the Gemara.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:4.hebrew: ואל יאמר בלבו: ״אומנות זו אינה מעשרת״, אלא יבקש רחמים למי שהעושר שלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:6:4.english: And he should not say in his heart: “This trade does not enrich [one]”; rather, he should pray for mercy to the One to Whom wealth belongs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:1.hebrew: חמר גמל ספן קדר - בעלי קרנות. כל אלו אומנות ליסטיות: כשלנים בדרכים, הם נכנסים ולוקטים עצים מן הכרמים ופירות; ועוד, שנשכרים לאדם ומעבירין על תנאם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:1.english: A donkey driver, a camel driver, a sailor, [and] a potter - [These are] people of the crossroads. All of these are trades of robbery: when they lodge on the roads, they enter and gather wood and fruit from the vineyards; and furthermore, they are hired by a person and violate the terms of their agreement.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:2.hebrew: רועה - בהמות שלו, שמעבירן לרעות בשדה אחרים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:2.english: A shepherd - [A shepherd of] his own animals, who leads them to graze in the fields of others.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:3.hebrew: חנוני - מלומד באונאה — להטיל מים ביין, צרורות בחטין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:3.english: A storekeeper - [He is] practiced in fraud: putting water into wine, [and] pebbles into wheat.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:4.english: In his name - Of Abba Gurya.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:5.english: Most donkey drivers are wicked - Because of [their] robbery.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:6.hebrew: הגמלין רובן כשרים - שפורשין למדברות, למקום גדודי חיות וליסטין, ויראים לנפשם, ומשברים לבם למקום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:6.english: Most camel drivers are of fit character - For they venture into the deserts, to a place of bands of wild beasts and bandits, and they fear for their lives and break their hearts before the Omnipresent:

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:7.hebrew: הספנין רובן חסידים - שפורשין למקום הסכנה, ותמיד הם ברעדה יותר מן הגמלין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:7.english: Most sailors are pious - For they set sail to a place of danger, and they are always in trembling, more than the camel drivers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:8.hebrew: טוב שברופאים לגיהנם - אינו ירא מן החולי, ומאכלו מאכל בריאים, ואינו משבר לבו למקום; ופעמים שהורג נפשות; ויש בידו לרפאות העני, ואינו מרפא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:8.english: The best of doctors is to Gehenna - He does not fear illness, and his food is the food of healthy people, and he does not humble his heart before the Omnipresent; and at times he kills people; and it is in his power to heal the poor person, yet he does not heal [him].

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:9.hebrew: טוב שבטבחים - ספיקי טריפות באות לידו, וחס על ממונו ומאכילן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:8:9.english: The best of butchers - Cases of doubtful tereifot come into his hands, and he spares his money and feeds them [to others].

Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:9:1.hebrew: אבל התורה אינה כן - שאף הבא לידי זקנה או ייסורין, ואינו יכול לעסוק בה, הוא אוכל ממתן שכרה, דכתיב: "עוד ינובון בשיבה":
Rashi on Kiddushin 82a:9:1.english: But the Torah is not so - For even one who comes to old age or suffering and is unable to engage in it, he partakes of the reward granted for it, as it is written: “They shall still bring forth fruit in old age” (Psalms 92:15).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:1:1.hebrew: הכל לשם שמים - ועל זו אנו סומכין השתא, שאנו משתמשים בנשים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:1:1.english: "All is for the sake of Heaven" - And upon this [statement] we rely nowadays, that we make use of [the services of] women.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:2:1.hebrew: לא ילמד רווק סופרים - פי': תלמידים. "רווק" — הוא אדם פנוי שלא נשא אשה מעולם, ותרגום של "ובחורים כשול יכשלו" הוא "רווקים" (ישעיהו מ׳:ל׳):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:2:1.english: "A bachelor may not teach soferim" - Explanation: [This means] students. A "bachelor" [ravak] is an unmarried man who has never married a woman. And the translation of "and young men shall utterly stumble" is ravakim (Isaiah 40:30).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:2:2.english: "Nor may [a bachelor] herd cattle" - Because he has greater lust than another man who has married a woman.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:5:1.english: "Nor may [a bachelor] herd an animal" - Because he has greater desire than another man who has married a woman.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:6:1.hebrew: לא יתייחד עם הנשים - פי' בקונט': ואפילו עם נשים הרבה, ודווקא רוכל, אבל איש אחר — מותר. וקשה להר"ם, דאמר לעיל (קידושין דף פא.): "אנשים מבפנים ונשים מבחוץ — חוששין משום יחוד", משמע דאסור להתייחד עם נשים הרבה לכ"ע! לכן נ"ל: "לא יתייחד עם הנשים" — אפילו אשתו עמו, דשרינן לעיל (קידושין דף פ:); דכיון דהוי רוכל, איכא חששא טפי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:6:1.english: "He may not be secluded with women" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Even with many women; and specifically [with regard to] a peddler, but another man is permitted. But this is difficult to the Ram [Rabbeinu Meir], as [the Gemara] said above (81a): "[If] men are inside and women are outside, we are concerned for seclusion," which implies that it is prohibited to be secluded with many women according to everyone! Therefore, it appears to me [that the Mishnah means]: "He may not be secluded with women" — even [when] his wife is with him, which we permitted above (80b); for since he is a peddler, there is a greater concern.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:6:2.hebrew: אלא הכל לפי זכותו - פירוש: לפי מזלו, דבני וחיי ומזוני לאו בזכותא תליא מילתא, אלא במזלא תליא מילתא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 82a:6:2.english: "Rather, all is in accordance with his merit" - Explanation: According to his constellation [mazal], for children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, but rather the matter depends on constellation.
